description: A Mediterranean-inspired restaurant dining alcove photographed at standing eye-level with a normal lens, capturing a three-quarter view of the dining table set within an arched plaster niche. The architecture features deeply curved barrel-vault arches in rough white plaster, creating an intimate grotto-like space. A warm light oak dining table with turned legs is surrounded by four upholstered dining chairs in a cream-on-cream geometric woven fabric with natural wood frames. The table is formally set with wine glasses, dark charcoal linen napkins, white ceramic plates, and polished silver flatware. A shallow white ceramic serving piece sits at center. The back wall within the arch is lined with hand-painted geometric encaustic tiles in a blue-white-buff triangular pattern — each square divided into four triangles with alternating cobalt and cream. Two natural oak open shelves span the tile back wall, displaying a raw clay amphora vase, a small white ceramic cup, and a model wooden sailboat. Below the shelves, a walnut sideboard or credenza forms a base for the display. The terracotta floor tile is in a classic small square Spanish format. On the left plaster wall, a circular warm-glowing ring form emits a soft halo of warm amber light. The mood is quiet and romantic with a warm Mediterranean character.
